page0.text:
I go back to my room and lie down.
Sleepiness spreads to my whole body as soon as I do.

page1.text:
...
I stare at the dark ceiling.
We are going to Illyasviel... That girl in white's hideout tomorrow.

page2.text:
No matter what kind of negotiations take place, it's obvious that it'll become a trial of strength.
Tohsaka suggested that we take a nap before we head over, since we won't be able to achieve good results if we go with tired bodies.

page3.text: "...Five more hours till dawn. We have to go talk to that girl after that."

page4.text:
The young Master that appeared in front of us on the night I became a Master.
If Saber is an excellent Servant in all aspects,
then Berserker is specialized when it comes to battle.
There's no Servant that can match Berserker simply in terms of battle.

page5.text:
"...How are we supposed to talk with such monsters?"
Saying it makes me believe that it's impossible to negotiate with them.
However...

page6.text:
Strangely, I don't feel any uneasiness.
I feel like that Illya kid will understand if we talk to her.
...Just like Tohsaka, I'm sure she can differentiate her enemies and allies as a mage, but I feel like she's a decent kid in a different regard.

page7.text:
"...Geez, what wishful thinking when I haven't even talked with her yet."
I bet she would flame me, saying that it's a convenient fantasy.
But, what's wrong with believing that?
Is it weird to have hope for someone who you don't know and are about to meet?

page8.text:
...
I realize that I'm gritting my teeth.
The man that told me to drown in my ideals betrayed Tohsaka in front of my eyes.
A guy with that much trust and power changed his beliefs that easily.

page9.text:
"...Archer."
I feel my heart start to sink.
No, is it freezing?
My mind freezes, just thinking back at his actions.

page10.text:
I'm angry.
I can't forgive him for betraying Tohsaka, out of all people.
I can't forgive him for abandoning his ally, out of all people.
I... Will never be like that.
Even if that had been the very best action to survive and it ends up being the correct path, I will never do something like that.

page11.text:
His actions have been getting on my nerves.
He told me not to talk about ideals.
I rebelled against him when he said that I can't save everything.
Even then... I agreed somewhere in my heart.

page12.text:
...His words are correct.
The hero of justice that my old man talked about was just a pipe dream,
and I accepted the fact that I have to become like him if I wanted to get as close to that ideal as possible.
I've been denying it, even though I had accepted it in my mind.

page13.text:
...But, this time isn't that kind of level.
I can't accept him.
I can't accept the action that he took no matter the circumstances.
I won't be able to keep standing if I approve of it.

page14.text:
"...That's why I can't lose to you."
...My words don't disperse into the night and remain in the room.
A few more hours until dawn.
I keep repeating those words in my mud-like slumber...
